questions.explanation: This problem tests two core skills: designing DP state with auxiliary dimensions and implementing path reconstruction. The O(n²·k) transition captures the fundamental challenge—selecting the optimal previous index while maintaining sequence order. Key concepts include using a "last index" dimension to enforce ordering, incorporating transition costs between consecutive selections, and leveraging parent pointers for reconstruction. The space-time trade-off is natural here: O(n·k) space stores the optimal substructure, while the O(n²·k) computation is necessary to evaluate all candidate transitions during DP construction.
